references.text: The Lord said to my lord: Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet. Both texts speak of victory over enemies and the symbolic image of placing one's feet on the enemy's neck or making them a footstool.

Blessed is Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the Lord? He is your shield and helper, your victorious sword. Your enemies will bow down before you, and you will tread upon their heights. The theme of treading on enemies as a sign of complete victory.

I will give them into your hand who oppressed you, those who said to you: Bow down so we can walk over you! And you made your back like the ground, like a street for those who walked over it. The image of subduing enemies by treading on them.
The five kings fled and hid in the cave at Makkedah. It was reported to Joshua that the five kings had been found, hidden in the cave. The context of the event where the kings were brought out.

Joshua said to them: Do not fear or be afraid! Be strong and courageous! For this is how the Lord will do with all your enemies whom you fight against. The continuation of this event where Joshua encourages the leaders.
Kings were bound in chains and princes in iron fetters. The theme of defeated kings being humbled and subjugated.
The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. A New Testament parallel about crushing enemies underfoot as a sign of final victory.
For he must reign until God has put all his enemies under his feet. Christ's rule is described with the same image of enemies under his feet.
